entries.title: The Thinking Machine
entries.author: Stephen Witt
entries.takeaway: The history left me thinking about how accidents and luck shape what we later call a strategy.
entries.liked: I enjoyed the history of GPUs alongside the portrait of Jensen Huang. The technical history made the company story more interesting for me.
entries.post_title: The Thinking Machine, and making room for luck

entries.title: The Elements: A Visual Exploration of Every Known Atom in the Universe
entries.author: Theodore Gray
entries.liked: The surprising everyday facts, such as the zinc roofs of Paris, and many others.

entries.title: Atomic Habits
entries.author: James Clear
entries.takeaway: Clear connects small, repeatable actions with the identity and habits they build.

entries.title: Think Faster, Talk Smarter
entries.author: Matt Abrahams
entries.takeaway: Abrahams offers structures for speaking when there is no time to prepare.

entries.title: Think Like a Monk
entries.author: Jay Shetty
entries.takeaway: Shetty brings ideas from monastic practice into questions about attention, identity and purpose.

entries.title: 12 Rules for Life
entries.author: Jordan B. Peterson
entries.takeaway: Peterson frames responsibility and meaning as responses to uncertainty and suffering.

entries.title: Surrounded by Idiots
entries.author: Thomas Erikson
entries.takeaway: Erikson uses a four-colour personality model to discuss communication differences.

entries.title: Algorithms to Live By
entries.author: Brian Christian and Tom Griffiths
entries.takeaway: Computer-science problems offer ways to think about decisions with limited time and information.

entries.title: Breath
entries.author: James Nestor
entries.takeaway: Nestor explores breathing through reporting, history and personal experiments.

entries.title: Glucose Revolution
entries.author: Jessie Inchauspé
entries.takeaway: Inchauspé examines how everyday eating patterns relate to changes in blood glucose.

entries.title: High on Life
entries.author: David JP Phillips
entries.takeaway: Phillips presents a neurochemical framework for thinking about mood and motivation.

entries.title: The Ageless Brain
entries.author: Dale E. Bredesen
entries.takeaway: Bredesen sets out his approach to brain ageing and prevention.

entries.title: Bringing Up Bébé
entries.author: Pamela Druckerman
entries.takeaway: Druckerman compares approaches to parenting through her observations of French family life.

entries.title: Hunt, Gather, Parent
entries.author: Michaeleen Doucleff
entries.takeaway: Doucleff explores cooperation and learning through observations of parenting across cultures.

entries.title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
entries.author: Philippa Perry
entries.takeaway: Perry places relationships, understanding feelings and repairing mistakes at the centre of parenting.

entries.title: Sapiens
entries.author: Yuval Noah Harari
entries.takeaway: Harari traces how shared stories make large-scale human cooperation possible.

entries.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
entries.author: Jared Diamond
entries.takeaway: Diamond argues that geography and environments shaped the unequal development of societies.

entries.title: Humankind
entries.author: Rutger Bregman
entries.takeaway: Bregman asks what changes when institutions begin with a more hopeful view of people.

entries.title: Nexus
entries.author: Yuval Noah Harari
entries.takeaway: Harari distinguishes the power of information networks from their ability to produce truth.

entries.title: Invisible Women
entries.author: Caroline Criado Perez
entries.takeaway: Criado Perez examines what happens when data and design treat men as the default.

entries.title: The End of Capitalism
entries.author: Ulrike Herrmann
entries.takeaway: Herrmann questions whether continued economic growth can fit within environmental limits.

entries.title: Talous ja humanismi
entries.author: Sixten Korkman
entries.takeaway: Korkman places economics alongside humanist questions about values and society.

entries.title: AI Engineering
entries.author: Chip Huyen
entries.takeaway: Huyen puts evaluation at the centre of building applications with foundation models.

entries.title: The Worlds I See
entries.author: Fei-Fei Li
entries.takeaway: Li connects the history of computer vision and ImageNet with the case for human-centred AI.

entries.title: If It's Smart, It's Vulnerable
entries.author: Mikko Hyppönen
entries.takeaway: Hyppönen examines the security and privacy trade-offs of connecting everyday things to the internet.

entries.title: We Are Bellingcat
entries.author: Eliot Higgins
entries.takeaway: Higgins explains how public information and verifiable evidence support open-source investigations.

entries.title: Permanent Record
entries.author: Edward Snowden
entries.takeaway: Snowden recounts his work inside intelligence systems and his decision to expose mass surveillance.

entries.title: Elon Musk
entries.author: Ashlee Vance
entries.takeaway: Vance follows Musk's companies and the risks involved in building them.

entries.title: Can't Hurt Me
entries.author: David Goggins
entries.takeaway: Goggins connects his life story with his ideas about discipline and endurance.

entries.title: The Happiest Man on Earth
entries.author: Eddie Jaku
entries.takeaway: Jaku reflects on kindness, friendship and gratitude in his memoir of survival.

entries.title: I May Be Wrong
entries.author: Björn Natthiko Lindeblad
entries.takeaway: Lindeblad reflects on uncertainty and learning to let go of thoughts.

entries.title: Empire of AI
entries.author: Karen Hao
entries.takeaway: The race towards AGI, the economic incentives and the labour behind AI stood out to me.

entries.title: How to Talk to AI (and How Not To)
entries.author: Jamie Bartlett
entries.takeaway: An introduction aimed at people who are less immersed in AI.
entries.disliked: Quite high level for me. A summary might have been enough.

entries.title: LLM evals — video notes
entries.status: Watched · original video link still to add
entries.takeaway: I want to keep developing my own judgement by looking at the outputs, rather than automating that work away.
